title: United States–Germany Strategic Energy & Industrial Partnership
subtitle: Where deeper industrial integration creates strategic value, through which instruments, and where to stay out
label: Generated from Allied Industrial Base Explorer data and a curated external evidence layer (accessed 2026-11-06); evidence, sources and caveats in the appendix. Data as of 30 October 2026.

inlines.v: Battery Materials & Cells: Synthetic graphite (anode-grade) (Germany->US); Natural graphite (joint); Other accumulators (joint). Electric Vehicles: Electric & plug-in cars (Germany->US). Nuclear Fuel & Reactor Systems: Nuclear extraction (joint). Permanent Magnets & Drive Systems: Rare-earth oxides & compounds (joint); Ferrite & other magnets (Germany->US); Electric motors (Germany->US); Motor & generator parts (Germany->US). Semiconductors & Power Electronics: Power electronics components (Germany->US).

Recognise trusted partner supply of electric vehicles refining (rare-earth metals, rare-earth oxides & compounds); electric & plug-in cars; ferrite & other magnets in procurement and content rules. Bind market access for synthetic graphite (anode-grade). Keep uranium/fuel extraction: aggregated low-coverage sub-sectors (spent fuel & nuclear scrap, uranium ores); nuclear special materials; transformers open to global sourcing.
Upgrade US-EU critical minerals MOU and action plan (EU-level, applies to Germany): sector strategy, reciprocal commitments, a KPI dashboard and an annual review. No new MOU.

Do not co-subsidise new Electric Vehicles components (accumulator parts & separators, electric motors, ferrite & other magnets) capacity. Do not co-subsidise new Automatic controllers capacity. Do not co-subsidise new Electric buses, trucks & tractors capacity.

Of 142 technology x stage cells and electro-industrial nodes assessed for the pair, 45 show an active complementarity (a supplier meeting the other's need, a shared chokepoint, a capacity-constrained trusted supplier or a chain specialisation), 7 direct competition and 67 no strategic case. The relationship is not one of general similarity: most of the electro-industrial base needs no bilateral intervention.

AIB strategic roles: US Demand & Market Anchor (primary), Coordination / Bridge Hub (primary), Capital & Investment Anchor (primary), Scale Manufacturing & Integration Platform (secondary), Specialized Technology & Manufacturing Anchor (secondary); Germany Capital & Investment Anchor (primary), Scale Manufacturing & Integration Platform (primary), Demand & Market Anchor (primary), Coordination / Bridge Hub (secondary), Specialized Technology & Manufacturing Anchor (secondary).

Germany supplies synthetic graphite (anode-grade), electric & plug-in cars, ferrite & other magnets, electric motors where the US is short; the US supplies battery recycling feed, refrigerants, sensors & controller parts, ac generators where Germany is short; the two share exposure to the same coercive supplier in rare-earth oxides & compounds, natural graphite, other accumulators, li-ion cells & packs, rare-earth permanent magnets, copper smelting & refining, where neither can supply the other and the answer is joint demand, finance and third-country capacity.

From the AIB roles, the US brings demand and offtake, coordination across allied chains, capital; Germany brings capital, scale manufacturing, demand and offtake. Public finance runs through DOE LPO, DoW OSC, DFC, EXIM on the US side and KfW, KfW IPEX, Hermes, UFK, DEG on the Germany side. The trade is market access and demand certainty for trusted capacity.

Do not co-subsidise new Electric buses, trucks & tractors capacity: both are strong suppliers (US 15%, Germany 11%). More trusted capacity is needed, so agree who specialises in what rather than racing.
Existing mechanisms and the MEA question
. Gaps: no cross-sector KPI dashboard or review cycle; no bilateral mechanism covers SC-EV, SC-SEMIS, SC-GRID; USDE-M3 has no published project pipeline.
Do not sign a new energy MOU. Give USDE-M3 a sector strategy, reciprocal commitments and a KPI dashboard covering the recommended compacts, reviewed every 12 months.

This section sets out what already exists before anything new is proposed. Facts are from the curated evidence layer (accessed 2026-11-06); items marked partial or unverified rest on secondary sources and should be confirmed before citation.
Germany's memberships in OSI's economic-security agreements table: G7, MSP, NATO.
Germany and the USA are both original MSP partners and automatic members of the MSP Forum launched in 2024.

TTC (created 2021) had its future questioned under the 2025 administration; no formal termination or revival was found, so it is treated as dormant and superseded by the 2025 framework and 2026 critical minerals MOU.

G7 leaders (including the USA and Germany) launched the Action Plan at Kananaskis on 17 Jun 2025 to diversify production, encourage investment and local value creation; interested members support the Minerals Security Partnership; no named German-US projects.
In the OSI energy basket, US imported US$27.8bn from Germany and Germany imported US$26.8bn from US (bilateral flows 2024, summed over the technology x stage cells).

Parliament approved the main regulation on 16 Jun 2026 (440-151), governments adopted it on 25 Jun and EU tariff cuts took effect 1 Jul 2026; Parliament's position carried suspension and sunset clauses (sunset 31 Mar 2028).
Parliament suspended work on approving the deal on 21 Jan 2026 over US Greenland demands and tariff threats and unfroze it in early Feb 2026; the freeze is lifted, so status shown is historical.

Supreme Court held on 20 Feb 2026 that IEEPA does not authorise tariffs; a Section 122 surcharge (reported at 10%, then 15%) ran from 24 Feb for 150 days and could exceed the Turnberry 15% ceiling where MFN is zero (Bruegel); it expired 24 Jul 2026; sources conflict on the rate.

On 31 Jul 2026 the Commission removed the 6 Aug expiry and extended indefinitely the suspension of EUR 93bn of countermeasures (Regulation 2025/1564), under continuous review with the option to reactivate; page seen only as a search result.

GM terminated its long-term magnet supply agreement with e-VAC (reported 22 Oct 2026); the parties are reportedly in arbitration and the dispute dates from April 2026; one German source dates the notice to July 2026; reasons not stated by the parties.

Germany and the US signed an energy and climate partnership in May 2022 with work on LNG, hydrogen and offshore wind; no 2025-26 bilateral energy, hydrogen or critical-minerals agreement was found, and current activity is unconfirmed.

US applies the higher of MFN or a 15% all-in tariff on EU goods; the EU intends US$750bn of US LNG, oil and nuclear purchases through 2028 and US$40bn of AI chips, and European firms are expected to invest US$600bn more in the US; commitments mostly non-binding.

Rubio and Sefcovic signed a non-binding MOU on 24 Apr 2026 to diversify mining, processing and refining and coordinate on third-country export controls; a USTR action plan explores border-adjusted price floors and a later plurilateral club; no binding agreement or projects found.
Investment vehicle, project pipeline and financing
Corporate relationships in the recommended compacts

Siemens Energy announced a US$150m large power transformer plant in Charlotte in Feb 2024, originally for early-2026 output (24 units a year, rising to 57); a June 2025 report put US production at 2027.
e-VAC was awarded about US$112m in Section 48C tax credits for its US$500m-plus Sumter facility in April 2024.
Infineon agreed in Feb 2025 to sell its 200 mm Austin fab to SkyWater with a long-term supply agreement, reducing its own US wafer capacity (about 4,000 US staff remain).

Siemens announced more than US$10bn of added US investment in March 2025, including electrical-products plants in Fort Worth and Pomona (US$285m reported) and the Altair acquisition; the figure combines capex and an acquisition.
Siemens Energy announced US$1bn of US expansion across transformers, grid equipment and turbines, with a greenfield high-voltage switchgear plant in Mississippi (up to 300 jobs).

Mercedes plans a new Tuscaloosa model by 2027 (GLC localisation reported later); VW's Scout plant in South Carolina (about US$2bn) targets EV SUVs and pickups from late 2026-2027, while ID.4 output at Chattanooga was reported ending April 2026; sources conflict.

US-owned Tesla raised planned on-site 4680 cell capacity at Gruenheide from 8 to 18 GWh a year with about US$250m, cell output from H1 2027; the plant currently uses CATL and LG Energy Solution cells.
the US$800m figure is from a secondary source; publication date approximate.

BMW's US$1.7bn US programme includes a roughly US$700m Woodruff pack plant using Gen6 cylindrical cells from AESC (Florence SC) and iX5 production at Spartanburg, with series pack output reported for Dec 2026; publication date approximate.

US-listed Energy Fuels agreed on 23 Jun 2026 to buy 100% of Hanau-based VAC from Ara Partners (US$718m cash plus shares); close expected early 2027 subject to US and European approvals; price may adjust with the GM arbitration.

KfW's Raw Materials Fund (part of the Germany Fund) made its first two equity decisions, EUR 150m in Vulcan Energy (lithium) and EUR 50m in Arafura's Nolans rare earths project; a third is in due diligence and the target size is EUR 1.5bn; no US-linked project named; USD at about 1.16 per EUR.

German-owned VAC's Sumter plant (about US$500m, nearly 2,000 t/yr, operating since late 2025) shipped first magnets and held an opening ceremony in July 2026; about 90% of output was contracted to GM; expansion room reported up to 12,000 t.

Final investment decision in May 2026 after an Australian offtake commitment under the Strategic Reserve; construction began 8 Oct 2026; credit agencies from the US, Canada, Korea and Germany support it; the article's A$1.2bn figure is ambiguous.
Unverified items are left out of this section; they stay in the evidence register (evidence_register.csv) and the evidence layer.

Working channels today: US-EU framework trade arrangement and its 2026 legal basis (EU-level, applies to Germany) (finance); G7 Critical Minerals Action Plan and Minerals Security Partnership (a project pipeline). What the relationship lacks: no cross-sector KPI dashboard or review cycle; no bilateral mechanism covers SC-EV, SC-SEMIS, SC-GRID; USDE-M3 has no published project pipeline.
